name: Crazy Eights
description: Crazy Eights is a popular shedding card game, especially beloved by children. The objective is simple: be the first player to discard all your cards. Players take turns playing cards to a central discard pile, matching either the rank or suit of the top card. The eponymous "crazy" 8s are wild cards that can be played on anything and allow the player to change the suit.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: United States
Time Period: 1930s
Creator(s): Unknown (folk game)
Etymology: Named after the wild 8 cards that can "go crazy" and change suits
timeline: 1930s: Emerged as a variation of the older game "Eights" in the United States
1940s-1950s: Gained widespread popularity as a family and children's game
1970s: Influenced the commercial card game Uno, which was based on Crazy Eights mechanics
Present Day: Remains one of the most commonly taught card games to children worldwide

rules.objective: Be the first player to discard all cards from your hand.
rules.gameplay:
1. Starting Play: The player to the dealer's left goes first, then play proceeds clockwise
2. Taking Turns: On your turn, you must either play a valid card or draw from the stock pile
3. Playing Cards: Match the top card of the discard pile by rank, suit, or play a wild 8
4. Drawing: If you cannot play, draw cards from the stock pile until you can play (or draw one card depending on house rules)
5. Winning: The first player to play their last card wins the round
keyRules: Matching: A card must match the top discard card by rank OR suit (unless it's an 8)
Wild 8s: 8s can be played on any card regardless of rank or suit
Declaring Suit: When playing an 8, the player immediately declares the new suit to be matched
Stock Pile: If the stock pile runs out, shuffle the discard pile (except the top card) to form a new stock
Last Card: Some variations require saying "Last card" when down to one card

strategy.basic:
For Beginners
1. Save Your 8s: Keep 8s for emergencies when you cannot match the discard pile
2. Change Suits Wisely: When playing an 8, choose a suit you have multiple cards of
3. Force Draws: Play 2s strategically to make opponents draw cards
4. Pay Attention: Watch what cards other players are picking up to deduce their hands
5. Suit Management: Try to reduce the number of different suits in your hand
strategy.intermediate:
Card Counting: Keep track of which 8s have been played
Suit Control: Change suits to ones you know opponents don't have
Timing Reverses: Use Aces to give yourself multiple turns in 2-player games
Skip Chains: Coordinate Queens to skip dangerous opponents
strategy.advanced:
Bluffing with 8s: Play an 8 early to mislead opponents about your hand composition
Draw Pile Management: Control when opponents are forced to draw
Endgame Planning: Plan your final cards to ensure you can play out
Opponent Reading: Deduce opponent hand strength from their play patterns
